final_output.summary: Broker plan certified and ready trips created.

evidence_scope: Public Montreal location example; static road estimates and simulated van fleet. One live run is integration evidence, not calibrated route quality or production validation.

output.summary: 2 free vans for 2 deliveries; fleet snapshot frozen.

explanation.summary: Work order established from the frozen fleet snapshot: 2 selected deliveries (d-77b7e6295841a58c, d-9a3080d2e8662fa4) and 2 free vans (van2, van3), which are the only eligible vehicles. Any vans reserved or holding existing jobs are not in the free set, so their jobs remain locked and are excluded from this plan. The supplied evidence does not state depot origins, so they must be explicitly assumed and labeled as assumptions before routing; no GPS positions, live traffic, truck restrictions, fees or optimality are asserted. This is only the planning input, not a feasible dispatched plan. Route admission depends on deterministic tools and the independent certificate. A new plan is required if the delivery selection changes, the free/reserved fleet snapshot changes (a van becomes reserved, freed or unavailable), or depot origin assumptions change. Costs would be supplied CAD estimates; model API spend is tracked separately in USD. Passing delivery IDs, free van IDs and the snapshot reference to routing.

output.summary: Static directional road table captured for 6 nodes; no live traffic claim.

explanation.summary: Traffic role reviewed the frozen static directional OSRM driving road matrix for 6 nodes (input hash 9223a5516fa2f05e1cf45927afd11d0bd9c15dd08dc4e3e5b50db484c0cc3926). Times are static OSRM estimates, not live traffic, and do not establish heavy-truck suitability or account for municipal worksite delays. Limits: any unreachable pairs or snapped-location offsets must be taken from the matrix itself and are not asserted here. Only evidenced routing constraints (the 6-node directional matrix and the 2 selected deliveries with free vans van2 and van3 from the prior work order) are passed to optimization; depot origins are not evidenced and must be labeled as assumptions. This is a completed analysis input only, not a feasible dispatched plan; route admission depends on deterministic tools and the independent certificate.

Bounded comparison of 4 candidates (hybrid, one_truck:van2, one_truck:van3, separated); all 4 are feasible with valid independent certificates. The supplied evidence does not itemize per-candidate mandatory coverage, capacity, pickup-before-dropoff or deadline checks, so those are covered only by the certificate_valid flag and are not restated individually. The hybrid, one_truck:van2 and one_truck:van3 candidates tie at an estimated fleet cost of 5199 cents (CAD 51.99) and a makespan of 2497 s (about 41.6 min). The separated candidate costs 8363 cents (CAD 83.63), about CAD 31.64 more, and finishes sooner at 2257 s (about 37.6 min), a saving of 240 s. The selected best certified candidate in this bounded comparison is hybrid: it is the lowest-cost certified option, tied with the two single-truck options, and the evidence gives no tie-break rationale. The separated option is the faster alternative but at higher cost. Costs are supplied estimates, and the comparison does not claim global optimality. Times come from a static OSRM matrix, not live traffic, with no heavy-truck suitability or worksite delay modelling. Depot origins are not evidenced and remain assumptions. This is a completed analysis, not a feasible dispatched plan; route admission rests on the deterministic tools and the independent certificate. No delivery was omitted to reduce cost, since all candidates are certified feasible.

Its evidence refs ab6ea691-6ade-4523-b440-36d7ec23b535 and 5577bf3b-cd18-4cfb-a620-0fb803712c58 were not supplied to this role and are not cited here. Remaining gaps: no hash values or explicit problem/solution binding are visible, and no per-constraint breakdown is given. Times come from a static matrix with no live traffic or truck-restriction modelling. Depot origins are unevidenced assumptions. No global optimality is claimed.
